analysis.title: The Small Idea: Who Took Away the Punchbowl?
key_insights: Small caps ran more than 20% in Q2 2026, then reversed in Q3. The Russell 2000 fell more than 7% as investors rotated back to large cap growth tied to the AI buildout. The NYSE FANG+ Index rose 13% in the quarter.

Persistent inflation and ballooning government debt triggered a Fed rate hike in September 2026, and Treasury yields spiked to multidecade highs. Markets had been discounting an accommodative Fed earlier in the year, so the shift to higher-for-longer rates was rapid.

The hardest hit Q3 small cap groups were growth-oriented technology and industrials, including smaller data-center construction and supply-chain firms, because capex concentrated among the hyperscalers. Unprofitable, early-stage and long-duration names such as biotech also fell as higher discount rates reduced the value of projected cash flows.
Rising rates and crowding out by hyperscalers and the US Treasury limited access to capital and dampened hopes for speculative M&A premiums. Strategic acquisitions of small caps continued.

About one-third of Russell 2000 companies have more cash than debt. Half of the index's total debt sits in just 12% of market cap. The author argues stock pickers can avoid leveraged names and focus on self-financing, cash-flow positive companies.

Positive small cap returns have coexisted with rising yields in eight of the ten rising-rate periods since 1987 (rising defined as a minimum 95 basis point rise in the 10-year yield). The author argues that strong fundamentals can outweigh higher borrowing costs.

Small caps have high operating leverage, so a modest revenue increase can flow disproportionately to profit. Their domestic orientation helps under tariffs and onshoring, which benefit small cap industrials, heavy-equipment suppliers and engineering firms. New tax rules allow 100% year-one depreciation on certain property.

Earnings growth for Russell 2000 companies is projected to exceed the S&P 500 into Q4 2026 and through 2028. Excluding negative earners, the Russell 2000 trades at a 19% forward P/E discount to the S&P 500.

Some small cap energy companies trade at single-digit earnings multiples while benefiting from rising power consumption (including AI data centers), higher commodity-price floors and strong cash flow. Geopolitical conflict and tight petroleum and gas supply support upstream and midstream cash flows.

AI remains an opportunity for small caps. Data center buildouts need physical inputs from small providers of specialized hardware, HVAC equipment and industrial components, and AI tools that automate overhead can expand margins for small companies.

The team also sees opportunity in non-biotech healthcare, where valuations are compressed while cost structures normalize and earnings accelerate. The author expects the market to shift toward rewarding fundamentals over speculative narratives.

The author expects inflation to abate, the rate cycle to improve and geopolitical tensions to ease. The team is building positions slowly with price discipline and diversification rather than predicting which names will contribute.

sector_views.rationale: Single-digit earnings multiples, rising power demand including AI data centers, higher commodity-price floors and strong cash flow.
Tariffs, onshoring and 100% year-one depreciation help domestic industrials, heavy-equipment suppliers and engineering firms.
Compressed valuations while cost structures normalize and earnings accelerate.

sector_views.rationale: Hit hardest in Q3 as capex concentrated among hyperscalers, but the report sees physical-input demand as a continuing opportunity.

earnings_insights: Russell 2000 earnings growth is projected to exceed the S&P 500 into Q4 2026 and through 2028 (LSEG I/B/E/S consensus projection, data as of September 30, 2026).
Excluding negative earners, the Russell 2000 trades at a 19% forward P/E discount to the S&P 500 (Bloomberg, data as of October 29, 2026).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Persistent inflation and government debt led to a hike, and the market now prices higher-for-longer rates after expecting an accommodative Fed earlier in the year.
Higher discount rates hurt long-duration and unprofitable small caps and raise borrowing costs for leveraged companies.

macro_indicators.reading: Resilient, supported by robust business and consumer spending
macro_indicators.interpretation: Recession fears from higher rates have not shown up in activity data, which supports earnings growth.

risk_factors: Higher-for-longer rates hurt heavily indebted companies of any market cap.
Capex concentration among hyperscalers hurts smaller AI-related suppliers.
Access to capital is curtailed, and speculative M&A premiums are less likely.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows Russell 2000 trailing-year returns during periods of rising 10-year Treasury yields since October 1987, with rising periods defined as a minimum 95 basis point increase in the 10-year yield. The text says small caps had positive returns in eight of the ten periods.
vol_and_positioning: Investor preference rotated back to large cap growth tied to the AI buildout in Q3, with the NYSE FANG+ Index up 13% while the Russell 2000 fell more than 7%.
Hyperscalers and the US Treasury crowding out capital access is cited as a headwind for small caps.
geopolitical: Geopolitical conflicts and tight petroleum and gas supplies support global commodity export markets and cash flows for upstream and midstream operators.
Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty increased investor demand for defensive cash buffers that small caps cannot match.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong fundamentals and operating leverage can outweigh higher borrowing costs. Small caps rose in eight of ten rising-rate periods since 1987, earnings growth is projected to beat the S&P 500 through 2028, and the Russell 2000 trades at a 19% forward P/E discount.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher-for-longer rates after the September Fed hike hurt indebted companies and long-duration names. Capital is crowded out by hyperscalers and the Treasury, and recession fears persist.

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings growth and valuation discounts can outweigh the headwind of higher rates, especially for self-financing, cash-flow positive companies.
